newsitem.title: USA: Man suspected in U.S. balcony sex death released.
newsitem.headline: Man suspected in U.S. balcony sex death released.

text.p: A businessman arrested on suspicion of murder after an employee he was having sex with fell from a hotel balcony was released from custody on Friday, officials said.

The Los Angeles District Attorney's office said it found insufficient evidence to hold Robert Salazar, a 33-year-old Houston man, who failed to contact police after Sandra Orellana fell eight floors to her death.
Salazar, who worked for a Houston employment agency, went ahead with a scheduled business meeting the next morning and made calls to Orellana's room when she did not show up.

He initially denied knowing how Orellana, 27, had fallen. But after detectives found men's underwear and a man's shoe on the floor of her room, he admitted to having sex on her balcony but maintained the fall was an accident.

The D.A.'s office said in a statement that while Salazar's behaviour was suspicious, "there is no physical evidence to contradict his version of the events." Autopsy results showed no sign of trauma other than that resulting from the fall.
It said it might still consider bringing charges against him if results of sexual assault or toxicology tests conflict with Salazar's story.
According to Salazar, he had intercourse with Orellana in her room, after which she walked out on the balcony, clad only in a camisole, to admire the view.
He said he walked up behind her and began having sex again, at which point she pushed herself up on the railing of the balcony and tried to turn around, lost her balance and fell.
